reasons.a: Faulty fits the ridge logistic on all 896 rows and scores the AUC on the same rows: KAP23 L1.1 'No test set' (same data for training and testing), read in Section 2.4.
reasons.b: Fixed: stratified 5-fold CV of the same fit, held-out scores pooled, one AUC; the standard held-out evaluation and nothing else in the statistic.
reasons.c: Besides the CV block, the guard line differs: faulty returns None below 2 per class, fixed `n - (-(n) // 5) < 2` evaluates n + ceil(n/5) and returns None only for an empty class, so the fixed guard is laxer than the faulty one, the reverse of the fold minimum the note and CASE.md state (>= 2 per class per training fold, i.e. >= 3 per class); this difference is neither the error nor its correction (inert at the declared sizes).
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite indicators; class counts (an empty class in the fixed, below 2 in the faulty; both at or below the stated minimum); the Newton stopping rule on the step size inspects no input. Both MECH_CHECK lines judged: allowed guard, and the optimiser's convergence test.
reasons.e: No PB section 4 term in the brief (checked by script); no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: 896 country-years = the Muchlinski et al. out-of-sample test set in KAP23 Table A6 (896 rows, 19 positives, confirmed online); 30 indicators lie within the source's models (Muchlinski 90 variables, 70 of them with no values in the test set); under the caps.
reasons.g: Same classifier, AUC function, threshold 0.75 and decision rule; cost 1 fit vs 5 fits on 4/5 of the rows (the correction itself).
reasons.h: Brief states sizes, the axes and what each key measured, and the claim; 'new country-years' is what the estimand needs; nothing on country blocks or order (that is only in the world author's docstring).
reasons.i: Claim is AUC on new country-years; the fixed estimates AUC on rows not used for fitting.

repair_request: Criterion bodies only. Python parses `-(n_pos) // 5` as `(-n_pos) // 5`, so the fixed guard `min((n_pos - (-(n_pos) // 5)), (n_neg - (-(n_neg) // 5))) < 2` tests n + ceil(n/5) < 2 (None only for an empty class), while the faulty guard `min(n_pos, n_neg) < 2` returns None below 2 per class. Make the fixed guard compute the stated fold minimum, n - ceil(n/5) >= 2 (for example `n_pos - (-(-n_pos // 5))`), or use one and the same guard in both bodies. Nothing else needs to change.

The classifier (ridge logistic) is a typical one; the source names none.
reasons.b: Fixed applies the same oversampler to each training fold only and scores sensitivity on untouched original held-out rows: the standard correction.

reasons.e: No banned term; no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: KAP23 states no sizes for the oversampling example (P-2 reading 1); 400 x 12 is an ordinary clinical cohort size and within the caps.

reasons.i: Claim is sensitivity among new patients; the fixed estimates sensitivity on original rows not used in training.

reasons.b: Fixed: expanding-window forward evaluation (6 contiguous blocks, each of blocks 2-6 scored by a fit on the earlier blocks only), the standard correction.
reasons.c: Diff is the fold construction and the count of scored days, plus a None for an empty scored set that the forward structure needs; nothing else.
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite values; at least 2 per class in each fitting set (same line in both, listed in MECH_CHECK, allowed); empty scored set (fixed). No input inspection beyond these.
reasons.e: No banned term; no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: Source states no sizes for temporal leakage (P-2 reading 1); 500 days x 10 indicators is about two years of daily data, within the caps.
reasons.g: Same classifier, accuracy, threshold 0.58 and rule; 5 fits in both.
reasons.h: 'days in chronological order' is the axis named as setting ('time in order' in the text); 'later days' is required by the estimand.
